name: manual_757476
claim:
Formal graduation of .agent/memory/working/GITHUB_PERISCOPE_WATCHER_AND_AUTHORIZATION_2026-09-02.md into durable lessons.jsonl, plus a distinct addendum this working doc doesn't cover: a real hand-waving failure that happened in a separate session AFTER the fix was found, diagnosing the exact same underlying bug as "flaky" without ever tracing it. Two golden nuggets:

(1) Root cause and the correct diagnostic method, contrasted with what actually happened first: a Windows CI Go test failure (TestEnsureBackgroundServeReplacesIncompatibleDaemonAfterStartupWait, periscope) was initially diagnosed as a flaky/timing-sensitive test from a proxy signal alone -- it passed on one commit and failed on a later one, with zero Go-code diff between them (only unrelated docs changes existed in that diff), and the agent concluded "flaky, unrelated, just re-run it" without ever opening the actual assertion or tracing the watcher-cleanup code path. The user correctly rejected this ("even if we hit Re-run 100x, it will not fix itself. It is not flakiness"). The real root cause, found only by someone who actually traced the code: Windows cleanup called the native fsnotify Remove on a watch already invalidated by a prior remove/rename event, hanging watcher shutdown -- a genuine, deterministic deadlock reachable under a specific event ordering, not a timing coin-flip. Fixed by retaining ownership/budget cleanup while skipping the redundant native Remove call, with a regression test proving no second native removal occurs. General lesson: absence of a diff in the diagnosing agent's own recent commits is not evidence a bug doesn't exist -- the bug can predate that diff entirely, and a passing/failing sample of one commit each is never sufficient evidence to distinguish "flaky" from "deterministic but rarely exercised by CI's actual scheduling." Never conclude "flaky, just retry" without having read what the test actually asserts and traced the code path it exercises. This is now recorded as a third example under orama-system's own AFRP Failure Mode 7 (Handwaving/Proxy Conclusion), bin/orama-system/afrp/failure-modes.md, commit f67c2f1b -- cross-reference both records.

(2) PR-locality and non-merge discipline, plus connector-vs-PAT authorization diagnosis, both already established via the working doc this formalizes: a discovery/investigation PR (periscope #49) accumulating a real production fix does not thereby become authorized to merge -- discovery, publication, review, and merge authorization are four distinct decisions, and "save/commit/push/publish/fix" never implies "merge." Separately: GitHub write capability must never be inferred from a displayed user role or a repository-metadata field (e.g. admin/push access reported) -- the exact API boundary needed must be probed directly, since repository-contents write, pull-request-metadata write, review-thread resolution, and merge are four separate, independently-grantable permissions. Confirmed directly this session and the session before: a GitHub App/connector token can report admin access yet still return 403 on Contents writes (installation-token scope limitation, not branch protection or a code issue); a backup PAT can successfully write Contents commits yet still return 403 on PR-metadata/merge operations (Resource not accessible by personal access token) -- implementation permission does not imply PR-metadata or merge permission, and this boundary must be diagnosed and reported precisely rather than worked around or silently retried.

decisions.notes: Graduates a thorough existing working doc into durable lessons.jsonl per direct request, plus records a real hand-waving failure from a separate session diagnosing this exact bug as flaky -- both genuinely absent from the formal lesson system until now.
